owner_name: Sheffield United group (COH Sports, Steven Rosen and Helmy Eltoukhy)
note: Prince Abdullah bought Bramall Lane and other property back from Kevin McCabe's interests in 2020 after their court case, reuniting ground and club. COH Sports bought the club in December 2024 for about £105m including all real estate (Bramall Lane, Shirecliffe, hotel); the ground carries a mortgage to Emirates Bank per earlier reports.
The council built and owns the stadium; Doncaster Rovers took a 99-year operating lease in 2012 to run it. The Eco-Power naming deal ends after 2025-26, so the name may change.

After the 2011 administration Plymouth City Council bought the freehold for £1.6m and leased it back for 30 years. Under James Brent and then Simon Hallett the club bought the freehold back from the council for £2.7m (exact completion year not confirmed in the sources seen, after 2016).
sources: https://democracy.plymouth.gov.uk/documents/s48897/Home Park Football Stadium and Higher Home Park.pdf

owner_name: Wigan Council (land freehold); stadium leasehold held by a Mike Danson stadium company
lease_note: Stadium building held on long lease from the council; term not found
note: Wigan Council owns the freehold of the land. Owner Mike Danson has moved the stadium into its own company, separate from Wigan Athletic and Wigan Warriors, so the stadium interest would not pass automatically with the football club.

lease_note: Club holds a lease from the council; term not found
note: Cheltenham Borough Council owns the land and leases the ground to the club. In 2019 the council approved a land swap that changes the leased area on the terms of the existing lease.

lease_note: Club pays rent to the council; term not found
note: Wyre Borough Council owns Highbury and Fleetwood Town pay rent. The Pilley family rebuilt the stands after 2004 but did not take the freehold.

owner_name: Rochdale AFC (stadium company 100% owned by the club)
note: In 2016 Rochdale AFC bought out Rochdale council's and the Rugby League Facilities Trust's shares in the stadium company, giving the club 100% ownership; Rochdale Hornets are long-term tenants. The Ogden family bought the club in May 2024 and the ground stays inside the club group.

owner_name: County Ground Stadium Custodians Ltd (50% club/Clem Morfuni side, 50% TrustSTFC supporters' trust)
lease_note: 250-year lease back to the club from March 2023
note: On 24 March 2023 a joint venture of the club side and the supporters' trust bought the County Ground from Swindon Borough Council for £2.3m (funded by the Nigel Eady Trust) and leased it back to the club for 250 years. Reports differ on whether the non-trust half sits with the club or with owner Clem Morfuni personally; either way half is held by the trust, separate from the club.

lease_note: 30-year lease approved in 2018 at £25,000 a year before community-benefit discount (end year estimated from 2018 approval)
note: Meadow Park is a council-owned public park and the club leases the main ground and a second parcel from Hertsmere. The council approved a 25-year lease in 2013 and replaced it with a 30-year lease in 2018.

lease_note: Club operates/uses the ground under arrangement with the council; terms not found
note: Calderdale Council owns The Shay and decided in 2024 to stop running it. Its March 2025 decision to sell to Huddersfield Giants owner Ken Davy drew a legal challenge from Friends of The Shay, and Davy later withdrew, so the council still holds it and its future remains unsettled.
